content.markdown:
# Targeted sampling of small salinity pockets on Tisa floodplain fields

## Verified facts
- TloCare reports that its four-hectare sampling grid misses salinity pockets of 0.3–0.8 hectares. Blanket densification increases fieldwork, laboratory costs and delivery time; the company wants to predict variable zones before dispatching its sampling team. [F1]
- TloCare reports GPS coordinates and laboratory results for about 18,000 points over ten years. Its listed routine outputs cover pH, phosphorus, potassium, humus and liming needs, rather than explicitly establishing an archive of salinity reference measurements. [F2]
- TloCare reports poor early-spring NDVI guidance because salinity was not clearly visible. It describes field sensing as a planned introduction within two years, not as established company equipment. [F3]
- TloCare has two programmers and one GIS specialist who can devote up to one-third of their working time to new functions. Its existing environment includes PostGIS and a Django portal backend. [F4]
- Kosanović is open to joint company projects and prefers genuine field collection. His EM38 and pXRF equipment is available to external partners subject to scheduling and consumables cost recovery. [F5]
- Kosanović’s published work applied regression-kriging to a commercial sunflower farm using EM38 conductivity and pXRF sodium covariates. This supports testing sensor-assisted zoning, rather than assuming that EM38 alone reproduces the published approach. [F6]
- His sample-reduction study reports unstable nugget estimates below 30 samples, compromising kriging weights. His flooded-field study reports that transition zones require repeat measurements. Both findings identify risks to reducing sampling and relying on a single survey. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could establish whether targeted sensing finds the pockets its grid misses without increasing routine service cost or delivery time, and identify when repeat surveys undermine that case.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement, the project could provide floodplain field measurements for testing small-pocket detection, sensor transfer and calibration-sample tradeoffs under a commercial sampling constraint.

## Our inference
- This suggests a plausible joint project, conditional on confirming Kosanović’s project availability, which remains unknown. Local calibration is essential: results elsewhere in Vojvodina do not establish detection of TloCare’s small floodplain pockets or explain sunflower losses on these fields.
- An initial conductivity survey could guide later targeted sampling, but likely cannot meet a literal requirement for recommendations before any field visit. Historical records should not be treated as current salinity ground truth without checking analytes, depths, dates and methods.
- A lightweight GIS workflow likely fits better than a new software platform. Savings remain uncertain because sensor access, calibration, repeat surveys and integration may offset fewer laboratory analyses.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a pilot on previously investigated problem fields. TloCare would supply field access, records and workflow costs; Kosanović would design sensing, calibration and validation. Compare the current four-hectare grid, EM38-assisted regression-kriging and EM38-plus-pXRF regression-kriging. Separate tuning and spatially held-out evaluation samples, checking independence. Obtain laboratory references across suspected pockets and randomly selected predicted-positive and predicted-negative areas; count uncertain cases separately. Measure confirmed-pocket recall at 0.3–0.8 hectares, false-positive area, salinity error, uncertainty, total operational cost per hectare and turnaround, separating one-off validation expenditure. Negotiable go/no-go targets for the best configuration, whichever it is, are at least 90% confirmed-pocket recall, no higher operational cost and no slower delivery than baseline, with targeted—not blanket—routine densification. Proceed only if recommendations meet the agreed pre-dispatch interpretation, repeat-survey costs are included, and implementation fits stated staff capacity. Otherwise revise or stop deployment.
- Propose an eight-week pilot after access and scheduling are agreed: audit records and protocols first, then field collection, modelling and held-out evaluation. Agree salinity definitions and reference-map resolution before collection. Check moisture and flooding conditions, repeating transition-zone measurements if feasible; any claim of seasonal reuse would remain conditional on further testing.
- After evaluation, test reduced calibration designs without reusing held-out references for tuning. Propose delivery of sampling coordinates, salinity zones and uncertainty layers into PostGIS, with a minimal portal view. Estimate integration effort, equipment charges and maintenance before committing to deployment.

## Open questions
- Can Kosanović confirm availability for the joint project’s fieldwork and analysis, including instrument scheduling and charges?
- Can TloCare authorise pilot-field access, independent reference sampling and an audit of archived analytes, depths, dates, methods and data-sharing permissions?
- What salinity definition, missed-pocket tolerance, false-positive tolerance, cost ceiling and delivery deadline should replace or confirm the proposed decision targets?
- Does pre-dispatch prediction permit an initial sensor campaign reused later, or must recommendations rely entirely on existing data?

proposedActions: Propose an initial four-week field-to-model test, subject to the current legal timetable and procurement feasibility. Compare the 1993-sketch conceptual baseline with surveyed groundwater heads, borehole sediments and quality-assured leachate/groundwater COD, chloride, ammonium and conductivity. Use separate tuning and later evaluation rounds, checking their independence. Test local hydraulic properties rather than importing published values. A negotiable screening target is head error below 10% of surveyed head range on withheld observations, reporting measurement uncertainty and unresolved plume boundaries. Go/no-go would concern the best configuration tested, not a named model: proceed only if evidence supports defensible well placement, resources and authorised delivery are available, and four installed wells plus an inspectorate-accepted containment/treatment proposal remain achievable by the verified deadline. Otherwise escalate immediately for regulatory agreement and additional investigation rather than claim compliance.

Propose source-leakage controls alongside investigation, with safety and regulatory review. Compare site-leachate treatment candidates against an untreated control using separate tuning and evaluation aliquots. If ammonium warrants zeolite testing, measure breakthrough, hydraulic performance, COD and residual-management needs; negotiate concentration and capacity targets from inspectorate requirements before testing. Do not select treatment on ammonium removal alone.

Propose a funded scope covering drilling, surveys, external analyses, monitoring and documentation, with named authorised contractors and signatories. Agree seasonal follow-up and any additional investigation with the inspectorate. Assign operation, maintenance and collected-leachate responsibilities before recommending implementation.

are reading 0.18 mg/L manganese at the outlet of our coagulation stage across three different client sites.

Pre-oxidation with KMnO₄ at stoichiometric doses converted Mn(II) to colloidal MnO₂ prior to coagulation.

facts.text: Her continuous-flow iron–manganese study reported that, at a 1:1 Fe/Mn ratio, competition for coagulant capacity reduced iron removal by 12 percentage points.

inferences: This joint project is conditional on Žigić’s availability and reserved laboratory capacity, which remain unknown. Instrument availability alone does not establish analytical turnaround capacity.

The published oxidation–coagulation work suggests a useful experimental approach, not a validated greywater solution. Transfer from higher-concentration synthetic water requires real-matrix validation; the reported iron-removal tradeoff makes checking both metals essential.

The concentration discrepancy suggests investigating metal inputs, release and recycling alongside incomplete removal. Unmatched residence times, flows or analytical fractions could also explain an apparent increase; media release and tank cycling should remain hypotheses rather than assumed causes.
proposedActions: First, propose residence-time- and flow-matched stage sampling across all three installations, including recycle streams, actual greywater, reagents and fresh/spent media. Measure total/dissolved Mn and Fe, pH, dissolved oxygen and metal mass flows, using blanks, spikes and external confirmation. Use separate tuning and evaluation batches; check their independence. Against current-operation controls, run an explicit diagnostic matrix: unchanged reference; media contact only; tank redox/residence change only; reagent-batch substitution only; combined changes. Hold other factors fixed. Judge reproduction against the observed inlet-to-coagulation-outlet manganese increase, not an assumed mechanism; null individual effects narrow hypotheses without ending investigation. Then compare feasible oxidation/coagulation adjustments on real greywater and field-verify the best configuration. Proposed go/no-go requires evidence explaining the observed increase and an implementable change achieving Mn ≤0.10 and Fe ≤0.30 mg/L under the confirmed discharge sampling protocol, without major equipment replacement, within four months and before reinspection. Otherwise, do not claim readiness; report unresolved causes and feasibility barriers.

Confirm legal limits, sampling location and total-versus-dissolved definitions before acceptance testing; agree evaluation frequency and uncertainty handling before collecting verification samples.

Propose that AquaCikl’s engineers lead hydraulic mapping and safe operational trials, with its technician coordinating sampling. Subject to agreement, Žigić would lead experimental design and Faculty-led analytical interpretation. Arrange service-centre access, turnaround, external checks and costs before starting; nominate an operator to maintain and verify any selected change after the staffing window.

What legally applicable discharge sampling protocol, analytical definitions and current iron measurements should determine acceptance?

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The benchmark could establish whether PassengerView can meet its contractual arrival-accuracy target and identify data or deployment gaps before wider implementation.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement, the project could provide target-network telemetry for testing how state-space and recurrent predictors transfer to higher-frequency observations and operational display-level evaluation.

## Our inference
- This suggests a joint project could connect relevant forecasting expertise with an existing passenger-information product. The proposal is conditional: joint-project willingness is open, but current availability is unconfirmed and the stated collaboration capacity is limited.

Missing representative adverse-condition data would leave robustness unresolved, not passed.
- Propose a bounded extraction and stop-event reconstruction audit before scaling. Measure extraction throughput, reconstruction errors and missingness; establish whether Romanian coverage and confirmed disruption periods support evaluation. Use weather features only if historical and live availability can both be established.
- Propose a PassengerView shadow integration through Java/Spring and GTFS-Realtime on the company's on-premise containers. Pair company engineers with the researcher on reproducible preprocessing, retraining and monitoring; do not infer hardware fit from research benchmarks.

Document residual risks and security/performance costs of mitigations. Use actual KL-HSM hardware first; consider an SLE97 route only if justified and hardware access is agreed. Neither initial leakage screening nor the proof of concept would constitute certification.
